# Claude-BugHunter content attribution

Two explicitly abridged/reworked content adaptations only; no engine/code, toolchain, operational examples, executables, or complete skill collection is imported. Upstream identifies code as MIT (copyright 2026 Sachin Sharma) and documentation/skill content as CC BY 4.0. LICENSE-CODE and UPSTREAM-NOTICE are retained verbatim. LICENSE-CONTENT preserves the complete legal text, with only the trailing blank line normalized for Git whitespace checks. The new adapted content is distributed under CC BY 4.0; ARTEX code remains under its existing license. This is not a legal compatibility guarantee or endorsement.

adaptations.json pins exact original file hashes, upstream commit, attribution, adapted hashes and changes. Both adapted skill directories ship disabled/unbound: discovery is not authorization or execution. The administrator must review provenance, enable visibility through the existing agent UI, record the real installed content version, and explicitly bind it before managed runtime enforcement applies. No role field or default capability is invented.

Drive archive content is not copied: known skill organization informs the directory/version approach, but its per-skill redistribution licenses are not established. No original databases, credentials, binaries or unknown-license skill text is included.
